CheckTitle: Ensure MFA is Enforced for All SaaS Users
Benchmark: CIS Oracle SaaS Cloud Applications Benchmark v1.0.0
RequiredAccess: Identity domain REST API (read-only admin app role, e.g. Audit Administrator + Security Administrator)
Description: Every SaaS user should need a second factor to sign in. Native enforcement through identity domain sign-on policies works after the identity upgrade to OCI IAM; otherwise MFA must be enforced in the external identity provider. Phishing-resistant factors are preferred over SMS or email OTP.
Risk: Without MFA a stolen or reused password is enough to sign in.
AuditProcedure: Determine whether the environment uses OCI IAM natively or an external IdP.
On OCI IAM: Security Console > User Categories > Two-Factor Authentication shows MFA enabled for all categories; sign-on policy rules require MFA.
With an external IdP: confirm MFA is enforced there for all users.
Test a sign-in with a standard user and confirm an MFA prompt.

Steps: Enable MFA for all user categories (or in the external IdP).
Communicate enrollment and confirm enrollment via My Profile > Manage Secure Verification.
Test sign-ins to confirm MFA is consistently prompted.

DefaultValue: Not enforced for all SaaS users after the identity upgrade; not natively available before it.
Notes: Every identity domain user who can use a console password must have MFA activated (mfaStatus ENROLLED), using the OCI identity check for console MFA. Inactive accounts that fail are counted separately.
